prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell); proposes initial TOBT (Target Off Block Time), locks it at freeze horizon unless rule-based exception or authorized override recorded. Airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport keep safety authority. Parts: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM; Airport Capacity Plan, Acceptance Rate; no safety judgments); Slot Allocation Engine (Blueharbor; derives CTT (Calculated Takeoff Time); frozen CTT revisable on capacity update); Airport CDM Portal (Foxglove; confidence, reason codes; Common Situation Display states proposed/under negotiation/frozen/exempted; frozen change needs revised reason code, old value marked superseded); Tower Sequence Manager (alias Ironleaf; builds provisional runway order by runway, departure fix, wake category, spacing rule; executable departure order at Meridian Regional Airport); Departure Metering Service (aligns TOBT with CTT, sends CTT to TSM); Flight Data Exchange (flight intent data); North/South Runway Meter (separate queues); Surface Surveillance Adapter (at stand/movement area/holding short/committed); East/West Apron Sensor; Ramp Movement Board; Audit Event Ledger (prior/new value, user or function, timestamp, authority basis, operating state per change); Identity Access Service (only assigned roles approve frozen changes, exemptions, retrospective corrections); Performance Analytics Warehouse (compliance, delay attribution, negotiation effectiveness, rule quality); Time Synchronization Service; Weather Ingest Gateway (WIG, Orchard); Business Rules Registry (BRR); Collaborative Decision Log; Arrival Regulation Console; Contingency Operations Console; Airline Interface Adapter; Digital Briefing Room; Alert Distribution Hub; Sector Load Monitor; Gate Conflict Detector; Handling Resource Planner. Actors: Regional Flow Manager (Copperfin); Slot Coordinator (Halcyon); Airline Operations Coordinator (Saffron; confirms TOBT revisions before freeze); Ground Handling Dispatcher; Ramp Control Lead (Quartzline; pushback release priorities); Tower Supervisor (Brindle; owns departure sequence, may challenge CTT); Aircraft Operator Representative; Airport Duty Manager; Meteorology Briefing Officer; Data Governance Steward (audits samples); System Support Engineer. Items: TOBT, CTT, delay slip, Tactical Regulation Proposal, GDP status, Storm Cell Snapshot, Runway Inspection Note, Post Operations Report, duty coordination alert, Slot Compliance State, reason code, Stand Tow Request Form. Modes: Normal

New part:
S284: The Airline Operations Coordinator may request a sequence review when a flight has a valid operational reason to protect a connection, crew limit, or network rotation.
S285: The Slot Coordinator verifies that any proposed resequencing remains compatible with the Calculated Takeoff Time tolerance and the current Slot Compliance State.
S286: The Regional Flow Manager is notified when local resequencing threatens to erode the planned departure rate in the Airport Capacity Plan.
S287: Runway queue management favors stable ordering, but the Tower Supervisor may intervene when wake spacing, route restrictions, runway crossings, or emergency traffic require a change.
S288: Each manual sequence change is recorded in the Collaborative Decision Log with the user identity, timestamp, affected flight, and reason code.
S289: The Audit Event Ledger preserves the sequence history so that post-event review can distinguish operational necessity from avoidable volatility.
S290: Departure readiness checks combine aircraft operator status, ground handling status, cockpit readiness, route clearance availability, and surface position into a single tower-readable indicator.
S291: The Aircraft Operator Representative is responsible for keeping aircraft readiness information current enough for the tower team to trust the displayed status.
S292: The Ground Handling Dispatcher updates boarding, loading, door closure, and tow readiness milestones through the operational interface before the flight is considered eligible for pushback planning.
S293: Foxglove shall publish tower readiness changes to authenticated airline and handling users within the configured refresh interval.
S294: The Deicing Coordinator sends the Deicing Pad Queue Card when pad demand, treatment progress, or release timing changes.
S295: The deicing interface point exposes whether a flight still requires treatment, is waiting for pad access, is under treatment, or has been released for taxi within the protected time assumption.
S296: When deicing demand increases, the Tower Supervisor compares pad release expectations with runway queue gaps before accepting an aircraft into the active departure stream.
S297: During Adverse Weather Mode or a Capacity Reduction State, the Tower Sequence Manager applies the active spacing rules from the Business Rules Registry and highlights flights that may miss their Calculated Takeoff Time.
S298: In the Recovery Phase, the tower sequence workflow emphasizes measured acceleration rather than first-come recovery, because uncontrolled pushback surges can overload taxiways and recreate delay.
S299: Ground handling capacity is treated as a hard operational constraint because an aircraft cannot meet a feasible off-block time unless the required people, vehicles, and stand equipment are available at the stand before boarding closure.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
